findings.rule: REVIEW.md Framework rules: flag when the change has made CLAUDE.md outdated
findings.summary: The diff adds the Windows-only runtime dependency `tzdata` and makes `pip install -e .` the install that delivers it, so CLAUDE.md's Setup line (`python -m pip install pytest ruff polars`) and 'the one runtime dependency is `polars>=1.0`' are now outdated and on Windows no longer give a passing suite; the run may not edit CLAUDE.md or sdlc.yaml `commands.setup`, and plan.md names the replacement lines for the owner's guardrail PR, to merge after this change reaches main.

findings.rule: REVIEW.md: no test edits in a fix task
findings.summary: pre-existing test file modified in a fix-type change (REVIEW.md framework rule; build guide step 25)

The module-level `for _handler in (...)` loop leaves `_handler` bound in the module namespace after import. It does no harm, but `del _handler` or building the opener in a small helper would keep the module surface clean.

R5 (environment proxies still work through the hand-built opener) has no automated test, only the verifier's manual inspection of the handlers, so a later edit that drops `ProxyHandler` would still pass the suite.

The spec acceptance item 'python -m pip install -e . succeeds and git status stays clean (Linux)' is only partly proven: the build run's install failed on a read-only sandbox and the test run built a wheel instead, so the first full editable install is the owner's Windows check.
